sections.h2: Selling in Keller: the local picture
sections.html:
Keller covers 18.4 square miles of the Dallas-Fort Worth area and counted 47,516 residents on January 1, 2025. The city calls itself Texas's most family-friendly, and listings lean on that.

Old Town Keller and Keller Town Center are the two business districts. Buyers touring a house also ask about Big Bear Creek trails, The Keller Pointe recreation and aquatics center, the library and the senior activities center. Keller ISD is the school district, and the two main roads are U.S. Highway 377 (Main Street) and FM 1709 (Keller Parkway).

A house near either road gains convenience and loses some quiet. Describe that tradeoff honestly instead of letting a buyer discover it at the second showing.

Appraisals and exemptions for Keller come from Tarrant Appraisal District, while the city, the county and the school district each set a rate of their own. Seventy-three taxing units across Tarrant County rely on that one district, and there is no charge to file an exemption.

Hold on to your appraisal notice. If you sell after a protest was filed, tell the title company so the outcome is credited to the right person.

sections.h2: Keller tax dates and how a closing splits them
sections.html:
Keller's tax year turns on a few fixed dates, shown below.

Texas tax steps for a Keller owner
StepDate
Value and lien dateJanuary 1
Bills mailedAround October 1
First half of a split billNovember 30
Second half of a split billJune 30
Homestead applicationGenerally by April 30
Delinquent if unpaidFebruary 1

Ten percent is the most a homestead appraisal can rise in a year. The lien dates from January 1, so a buyer can inherit that year's bill, and the title company splits it at closing. Ask the Tarrant tax office for a current statement early.

sections.h2: Homestead and senior breaks when you move
sections.html:
A $140,000 homestead exemption comes from school districts, and a senior or disabled owner gets $60,000 more along with a cap on school tax. Anyone qualifying who downsizes within Texas may take a proportionate share of that ceiling along.

Before you list, ask the appraisal district to confirm exactly what carries over. If the seller never had the exemption, a buyer closing after January 1 may claim it right away.

The size of the disabled veteran exemption follows the VA rating, and it covers a single property the veteran owns. At a 100 percent rating, including by individual unemployability, the residence homestead can be fully exempt, and an unmarried surviving spouse may keep that benefit.

Smaller ratings bring smaller dollar amounts: $5,000 for a 10 to 29 percent rating, rising to $12,000 for 70 to 100 percent. April 30 is the usual filing date, though Section 11.22 applicants can have up to five years after the delinquency date. Ask Tarrant Appraisal District which forms to file and what it needs from the VA.

sections.h2: How a Keller owner can sell on a short clock
sections.html:
An agent, a private sale or a cash buyer: each one costs you time or money in a different way.

  • A listing in a high-value area can draw strong offers, but buyers expect clean inspections and often ask for repairs.
  • Going without an agent keeps the commission in your pocket and puts showings and contracts in your hands.
  • A cash purchase hands repairs to the buyer and closes on your date, useful after a job move, a divorce, a tenant problem or an inheritance.

Do your own math. Commission, repairs and the months of payments a listing takes all shrink what you net.

sections.h2: Closing and recording in Tarrant County
sections.html: Keller deeds go into the official records at the Tarrant County Clerk after a notary or similar officer witnesses the signature. Fees are charged per page, with records fees on top. Title companies usually handle the filing at closing. Do you plan a transfer on your own? Phone the clerk for the current fee schedule.

Heirs missing from the recorded deed must give the appraisal district a sworn statement of ownership, the death certificate and a utility bill, along with any court citation, before the exemption takes effect.

Depending on the facts, the new deed may be a transfer deed recorded before death, an executor's deed, a muniment of title order or an affidavit of heirship. Adding heirs to an old deed is not something a county clerk can do alone.

sections.h2: Tenants, a mortgage default or an open estate
sections.html:
All three add a step before closing. In a default, the lender's letter starts a short clock, and the auction falls on a first Tuesday at the courthouse. An open estate needs a court order or an affidavit before anyone can sign a deed. Renters need proper written notice, and a justice court handles the eviction suit.

Some cash buyers take a house with renters or an unsettled estate, though a Texas attorney should review the plan first.

sections.h2: Getting buyers past the first showing
sections.html: Resale houses in Keller compete with new construction in nearby cities, so have answers ready on school zoning, park access and trail links. Rankings matter less than the roof, the furnace and the drains, which an inspector will examine. Walk your lot first and fix what you can. Keep permits for past work close, along with your tax statement and any payoff letter, and a serious buyer can go from interest to offer without waiting on you. Answer questions about the neighborhood honestly, since buyers verify what they hear, and keep your lot tidy for the second visit, when many Keller buyers bring a contractor or a relative to look at the house again.

sections.h2: A Keller timeline from listing to closing
sections.html:
Think of the sale as three phases. In phase one, before the sign goes up, assemble the deed, your newest Tarrant tax statement and any payoff letter, and settle how much repair is worth the money. Phase two is the listing, when inspectors tend to scrutinize roofs, furnaces and drains and buyers push back. In phase three the title company searches for liens, divides the year's taxes and books a signing before a notary.

A cash buyer folds the first two phases into a single conversation. You accept a lower price and in return pick the date and skip the repair list. To choose between slow and fast, take the listing price, subtract commission, repairs and the months of mortgage, insurance and upkeep, and compare what is left with the cash figure.

sections.h2: Questions to settle before you sign
sections.html: Put identical questions to every buyer and the offers become easy to compare. Who covers the title policy? When is closing, and does the date slip if a loan drags? Will the buyer take the house with its flaws, or does an inspection reopen the price? Is financing needed or is the cash ready? Written answers head off the late surprises that stall contracts. With tenants or an estate involved, add one more: who clears the house before the keys change hands?

Tarrant County. Appraisals and exemptions come from Tarrant Appraisal District, and deeds are recorded by the Tarrant County Clerk.

faqs.q: Does Tarrant charge to file an exemption?
faqs.a: No. Filing is free, and most exemption applications are due by April 30.

faqs.q: What date makes a Texas tax bill late?
faqs.a: Most bills become delinquent on February 1, after being mailed around October 1.

faqs.q: Is a no-repairs sale possible in Keller?
faqs.a: Yes, through a cash buyer; a loan-backed buyer may still ask for repairs. Disclose known problems either way, and check permits on past work.
